svg.text: Backend for Frontend (BFF) Pattern — LLD
BFF Architecture & Request Aggregation
Problem: generic API returns too much/little data; client makes N sequential calls
BFF: thin server layer owned by frontend team, one BFF per client surface (web/mobile)
Aggregation: /dashboard → parallel fetch(users, orders, metrics) → compose response
Field selection: return only fields the client needs — reduces payload 60-80%
Fanout with Promise.all: concurrent upstream calls bounded by service SLA
Partial failure: if metrics service fails, return dashboard with metrics: null + error flag
Response shaping: rename/transform fields to match frontend data model exactly
Pagination translation: cursor-based upstream → offset-based if client needs it (rare)
Auth, Security & Token Management
BFF holds refresh tokens: httpOnly cookie → client JS never touches refresh token
Token exchange: BFF accepts session cookie → exchanges for service access tokens
Downstream auth: BFF injects Authorization header per upstream service call
CSRF: BFF validates SameSite cookie + optional CSRF token for state-mutating calls
Rate limiting: per-user rate limit at BFF layer — upstream services don't need to know
Request validation: BFF validates and sanitizes all inputs before forwarding
Secrets: BFF holds service credentials (API keys) — never exposed to client bundle
mTLS: BFF→services use mutual TLS; client→BFF uses standard TLS + session auth
Caching, SSR Integration & Edge Deployment
BFF-level cache: Redis/memory cache for repeated aggregations (TTL 30–60s)
Cache key: hash(userId + endpoint + query params) — per-user where needed
Stale-while-revalidate: serve cached response + async refresh for low-latency reads
SSR integration: Next.js server components call BFF directly (no client roundtrip)
Edge BFF: deploy at CDN edge (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge) — reduces TTFB
Edge constraints: no Node.js APIs, limited CPU time — keep aggregation logic simple
Streaming: BFF uses SSE/chunked transfer for progressive page hydration
Cold start: keep BFF warm via scheduled pings if using serverless (Lambda/Vercel)
Observability, Versioning & Trade-offs
Tracing: BFF propagates trace-id header to all upstream calls → distributed trace
Logging: log request shape, upstream latencies, errors — structured JSON to ELK/Datadog
Metrics: P50/P95/P99 per endpoint, upstream error rates, cache hit ratio
API versioning: BFF absorbs upstream breaking changes — shields clients from churn
Circuit breaker: wrap each upstream call — open after N failures → fast-fail + fallback
BFF vs GraphQL: BFF is simpler (REST endpoints), GraphQL more flexible but complex
BFF per surface: separate web-bff / mobile-bff — different payload shapes, versions
Anti-pattern: business logic in BFF — keep it data-shaping only, logic in services
Aggregate N upstream calls → 1 client request
Refresh token in httpOnly cookie, never in JS
Edge BFF reduces TTFB; SSR calls BFF server-side
Circuit breaker: partial failure → graceful degradation
No business logic in BFF — data shaping only
